title: Add retry/timeout presets + recommended production defaults
author: Ibrahim Khan
description: Context: As part of the Guided Onboarding / First Production Launch checklist, we want “production-safe defaults” in SDKs to reduce early support tickets (timeouts/retries, 429 surprises, and confusion around what the SDK does by default). Today the Python SDK defaults are effectively “no explicit timeouts + minimal retries,” which is risky in production and leads to confusing behavior under intermittent network issues. What’s in this PR: (1) Add first-class retry/timeout configuration primitives and named presets (interactive / production / batch). (2) Default new clients to a conservative, production-friendly preset (w/ an escape hatch to keep legacy behavior). (3) Document the recommended defaults and how to override per-client and per-request. (4) Add unit tests around retry policy, backoff/jitter, and honoring Retry-After for 429/503. (5) Update CHANGELOG with the new behavior and migration guidance. Presets (summary): interactive: short connect/read timeouts, low max_retries (good for CLIs/notebooks); production (default): connect_timeout=5s, read_timeout=60s, total_timeout=90s, max_retries=4, exponential backoff with jitter, retry on 408/409/429 and 5xx + transport timeouts; batch: longer read/total timeouts, higher max_retries but capped by total timeout. Notes/limits: We do NOT automatically retry streaming responses (SSE) in this PR; retries apply to request establishment. Streaming reconnect patterns will be documented separately and/or provided as helper utilities (tracked in ENG-5820 follow-ups). Telemetry: No new event payloads. We do add a lightweight User-Agent suffix for preset selection to help onboarding funnel attribution (value is one of: interactive|production|batch|custom). This is opt-out via client option. Risks: Changing defaults can be surprising; mitigated by (a) explicit docs + CHANGELOG, (b) REDWOOD_SDK_LEGACY_TIMEOUTS=1 env var to revert to prior behavior for one release cycle, (c) per-request override APIs.
commits: sdk: introduce TimeoutConfig, RetryConfig, and RetryPreset enum
sdk: wire presets into Client + request options plumbing
sdk: implement retry policy (status codes, transport errors) + Retry-After support
tests: add deterministic backoff tests w/ seeded jitter + mock transport failures
docs: update README + API reference examples for retries/timeouts
changelog: document new defaults + legacy env var escape hatch
notable_snippet:
Python usage example (README):

from redwood_sdk import Redwood, RetryPreset

client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"], retry_preset=RetryPreset.PRODUCTION)

# Per-request override
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    request_options={"timeout": {"total": 30}, "retries": {"max_retries": 2}},
)

# Legacy behavior (temporary escape hatch)
# export REDWOOD_SDK_LEGACY_TIMEOUTS=1
review_conversation: Monica Patel (2025-03-12): Defaults look reasonable, but I’m worried about silently retrying 409. Can you justify 409 being included? We’ve seen 409 on idempotency conflicts where retry might be okay, but we should be explicit.

Ibrahim Khan (2025-03-12): Good call. The 409 inclusion is primarily for idempotent POSTs where the first attempt succeeded server-side but the client lost the response. I updated docs to clarify and added a guard: only retry 409 when an Idempotency-Key is present (or when request is GET/HEAD). Added tests for both paths.
Brian Murphy (2025-03-13): Please ensure we honor Retry-After on both seconds and HTTP-date formats. Also cap sleep so we don’t blow past total_timeout.

Ibrahim Khan (2025-03-13): Implemented Retry-After parsing for int seconds + IMF-fixdate; if parsing fails we fall back to backoff. Also clamp delay to remaining total_timeout budget (and bail early if remaining <= 0). Added tests with frozen time.
Sabrina James (2025-03-14): Docs: can we add a quick table mapping presets to intended use? Also mention explicitly that streaming reconnect is not automatic.
Ibrahim Khan (2025-03-14): Added table + a callout box in README under “Streaming” explaining that retries apply to connection establishment only; reconnect patterns are app-managed for now.

Monica Patel (2025-03-17): One more request: make the legacy env var name consistent with other SDK toggles (REDWOOD_SDK_*). Also, please add a deprecation note that we’ll remove it after one release.
Ibrahim Khan (2025-03-17): Updated to REDWOOD_SDK_LEGACY_TIMEOUTS=1, added a NOTE in CHANGELOG that it’s planned for removal in 0.10.0 unless we see major regressions.

2025-03-17: Addressed requested changes (409/idempotency guard, Retry-After parsing, docs table/callouts)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Monica Patel (2025-03-18).
release_notes: Python SDK now supports retry/timeout presets: interactive, production (default), batch.
New config types: RetryConfig and TimeoutConfig; overrides supported at both client and request level.
Retry policy honors Retry-After and clamps delays to total timeout budget.
Temporary escape hatch: set REDWOOD_SDK_LEGACY_TIMEOUTS=1 to revert to prior default timeout behavior (planned removal after one release).
No automatic streaming reconnect in this release; retries apply to request establishment only.
